entry.label: Autopoiesis
entry.description: A network produces components that regenerate that network and constitute it as a distinguishable unity. The 1974 paper makes this a specific organisational condition, not a synonym for persistence.
entry.canonical_definition: Self-production of a unity through a recursively constituted network of component production.

profile.title: Autopoiesis
profile.summary: The biological account includes the production of a boundary that enables the processes producing it. Material turnover is compatible with the persistence of this organisation. The paper's biological use of autonomy concerns self-production of a unity. It doesn't establish the decision rights of its parts.
profile.canonical_definition: Self-production of a unity through a recursively constituted network of component production.
profile.why_it_matters: A boundary drawn by an analyst and a boundary produced by a living system make different claims.
practice_connections: Before applying the term, identify components, production processes, and boundary formation.
common_misreadings: Any durable feedback loop is autopoietic.
Calling an institution living establishes biological autopoiesis.
open_checks: Social applications need an explicit account of what is being produced.
Any organisational application must state its components, production processes, unit of analysis, and decision rights separately.
profile.editorial_note: Biological self-production and operational discretion are compared explicitly. This source-located distinction remains a candidate for editorial acceptance.

connections.scope_conditions: The paper defines autopoiesis through a network of component production and illustrates that organisation in a tessellation model. The illustration does not itself establish later biological or social applications.
